entries.subject: development-plan membership, material-consideration status, guidance status and operative/emerging source selection
ownerBoundaries: DPL-10 owns planning-source status and composition; source chronology alone never selects a policy winner.
DPL-05 owns generic typed target composition outside planning-specific authority.
entries.claimBoundary: Source/status coverage can identify what planning material exists and its authority class. It does not decide policy compliance, planning balance or permission.

entries.family: strategic design, context and site capacity
entries.subject: London strategic design-led approach, form/context response and bounded site-capacity questions
accelerationTriggers: known site/context condition appears capable of categorically defeating the controlled Reference House proposition
ownerBoundaries: Reference House identity and protected architectural order remain DPL-02 authority.
Site facts remain DPL-06 claims; planning may consume them without taking ownership.
entries.claimBoundary: The current London target represents selected Chapter 3 design obligations only. Family presence and bounded numeric checks do not establish acceptable planning design or site capacity.

entries.family: housing quality and accessibility planning policy
entries.subject: strategic dwelling quality, space, private amenity and planning-triggered accessibility category questions
accelerationTriggers: known planning requirement or candidate fact creates an obvious housing-quality/accessibility blocker at screening
ownerBoundaries: Planning may select an optional dwelling accessibility category; DPL-09/Building Regulations own technical Part M discharge.
Reference House human-factors and architectural decisions remain with their owning RH/HFI authorities.
entries.claimBoundary: Selected strategic housing standards are represented. This is not a complete housing-quality determination and does not prove Building Regulations accessibility compliance.

entries.subject: planning effects on neighbouring occupiers and relationships requiring contextual/evidence-led judgement
accelerationTriggers: known neighbour geometry/openings indicate an obvious potentially categorical amenity or privacy conflict
ownerBoundaries: DPL-11 owns neighbour/private-rights/process evidence; planning owns public-law amenity judgement.
Site neighbour geometry remains a DPL-06 claim and may feed both owners.
entries.claimBoundary: The registry exposes the planning family and evidence/judgement route. It does not calculate a universal amenity score or decide acceptability.

entries.family: transport, access, highway and parking planning policy
entries.subject: planning transport/access relationships, highway safety, parking/cycle provision and supporting evidence
accelerationTriggers: known street/access geometry creates an obvious categorical access or road-safety concern
parking/access facts are decision-critical for applicable local or strategic policy
ownerBoundaries: DPL-11 owns physical/legal access and rights evidence; DPL-08 owns building/site approach interfaces.
Planning owns transport/highway/parking policy applicability and judgement; a physically possible route is not a planning pass.
entries.claimBoundary: Croydon/Bromley supply bounded examples only. Bromley parking conflict remains unsupported where strategic/local temporal composition is unresolved.

entries.subject: listed/conservation/heritage designation applicability and planning effects on significance/setting
accelerationTriggers: credible designation or setting evidence could categorically defeat the controlled Reference House proposition
ownerBoundaries: The synthetic Reference Site's assumed absence of designation is a site-fixture assumption, not authoritative heritage evidence.
Planning heritage judgement remains distinct from architectural grammar/style preference.
entries.claimBoundary: An ASSUMED synthetic no-designation claim cannot become NOT_APPLICABLE_PROVED or a heritage planning pass.

entries.family: trees, landscape and urban greening planning policy
entries.subject: tree/designation retention, landscape response, arboricultural planning evidence and strategic greening duties
accelerationTriggers: known/protected tree or landscape condition dominates the only conformance-preserving placement
ownerBoundaries: DPL-11 owns arboricultural/ground physical evidence; planning owns tree/landscape policy consequences.
Historic TPO references never become current designation facts without current evidence.
entries.claimBoundary: Bromley Policy 73 is a bounded local example. It does not make tree status or all-London landscape judgement native.

entries.family: ecology, biodiversity and green infrastructure planning policy
entries.subject: habitat/ecology evidence, biodiversity policy and green-infrastructure planning consequences
accelerationTriggers: credible ecological/designation evidence indicates a potentially categorical site constraint
ownerBoundaries: Ecological evidence remains external/site evidence; planning owns policy consequence and balance.
DPL-11 ground/environmental evidence does not silently absorb ecological planning policy.
entries.claimBoundary: The canonical ecology claim is UNKNOWN. Registry presence does not provide habitat evidence, biodiversity calculation or planning acceptability.

entries.family: flood, drainage and SuDS planning policy
entries.subject: planning flood-risk, sustainable-drainage and water-management evidence/judgement
accelerationTriggers: known flood/sewer/drainage condition threatens the only conformance-preserving deployment route
ownerBoundaries: DPL-09 Part H owns Building Regulations drainage obligations; DPL-11 owns physical flood/water evidence; DPL-08 owns site-water interfaces.
Planning owns flood/SuDS policy applicability, evidence expectations and judgement without duplicating those other authorities.
entries.claimBoundary: Planning-family coverage does not select a discharge destination, prove hydraulic capacity or establish Part H compliance.

entries.family: air quality, noise and agent-of-change planning policy
entries.subject: environmental planning effects/evidence involving noise, air quality and sensitive-receptor relationships
accelerationTriggers: known severe environmental exposure or sensitive-receptor condition could defeat residential suitability
ownerBoundaries: DPL-09 Part E technical acoustic requirements are separate from planning noise/agent-of-change policy.
Environmental measurements remain site/external evidence rather than compiler-created facts.
entries.claimBoundary: The canonical external-noise claim is UNKNOWN. No planning-noise pass, exposure model or air-quality conclusion is inferred.

entries.family: energy, carbon and sustainability planning policy
entries.subject: strategic/local planning energy and sustainability duties distinct from Building Regulations technical compliance
accelerationTriggers: known planning energy/sustainability requirement forces a protected-order architectural change at the current decision point
ownerBoundaries: DPL-09 Part L/F technical compliance remains Building Regulations authority.
Planning energy/carbon policy may consume technical modelling evidence without becoming the technical target itself.
entries.claimBoundary: This family records planning coverage only; it does not perform energy modelling or establish regulatory/planning carbon compliance.

entries.subject: borough-specific explicit numeric standards whose applicability and authority are proven for the real site
accelerationTriggers: real borough authority is assigned and a bounded quantitative local policy is decision-critical
ownerBoundaries: Croydon and Bromley prove a common envelope, not common local numeric policy content.
DPL-RS-01 has no real borough target; no local numeric requirement may be invented for it.
entries.claimBoundary: Local numeric methods are site/borough-specific. Bromley Policy 30 remains unsupported where current strategic/local conflict semantics are unresolved.

entries.family: local qualitative and evidence-led planning policy
entries.subject: borough-specific character, backland, amenity, trees, road-safety, flood and other judgement/evidence families
accelerationTriggers: real borough authority is assigned and a known local policy family could categorically affect the controlled proposal
ownerBoundaries: The reusable borough seam is source/status/method/evidence composition only; substantive policy families remain local.
DPL-RS-01's explicit no-borough state is a coverage limitation, not permission to substitute an exemplar borough.
entries.claimBoundary: The two borough exemplars do not establish an all-borough ontology, judgement model or local-planning pass.

entries.family: planning validation, process and specialist evidence
entries.subject: application-validation information, specialist planning evidence and process material required by the selected authority/proposal
accelerationTriggers: known specialist evidence requirement is necessary to resolve a decision-critical screening uncertainty
ownerBoundaries: Validation/evidence requirements do not themselves determine policy compliance or permission.
Professional studies remain external evidence even where the compiler tracks that they are required.
entries.claimBoundary: This family records process/evidence coverage only and cannot manufacture specialist reports, validate an application or predict determination.

entries.family: emerging planning policy and material weight
entries.subject: emerging/non-operative planning sources and the judgement-led question of material weight
ownerBoundaries: Emerging source status can be represented; its planning weight is not a native numeric value.
An emerging source never silently replaces an operative development-plan source because it is newer.
entries.claimBoundary: The registry can prove a source is emerging/non-operative. It cannot assign scalar weight or promote it into operative policy.

entries.family: external planning determination, history and conditions
entries.subject: planning permission/refusal, appeal/history evidence and conditions imposed by competent statutory decision-makers
accelerationTriggers: existing proposal-specific planning history or condition is credible current evidence of a decision-critical constraint
ownerBoundaries: The compiler may record determination evidence but never grant/refuse permission or infer precedent as a reusable site rule.
Proposal-specific planning history is evidence, not a deterministic policy result for another proposal.
entries.claimBoundary: P6 remains external statutory authority. No P1–P5 family or registry metadata may manufacture a permission, refusal or condition.
